description:
Behavioral correlation that fires when a single source process accesses many distinct security/EDR product processes within a short window - the core behavior of an EDR killer such as TheGentlemen's GentleKiller, which terminates 400+ security processes across ~48 vendors in a loop. This detection is resilient to tool renaming, repacking and new BYOVD drivers because it keys on the killing behavior, not on file artifacts. Pair it with the BYOVD driver-load BROAD rule and the GentlemenCollection STRICT rule for full-confidence attribution. THRESHOLD CALIBRATION: the default threshold of 8 assumes a reasonably instrumented endpoint. If your environment only runs 3-4 security tools, the threshold may never be reached even during an active attack. Set the threshold to 50-75% of the number of distinct security processes running in your environment. Conversely, lower it to 4-5 for minimal stacks. BLIND SPOT: if GentleKiller injects into a legitimate process (process hollowing), SourceImage will show the host process (e.g. explorer.exe). The correlation still fires correctly but analysts must check SourceProcessId to identify the actual malicious thread rather than dismissing the alert based on the legitimate SourceImage name. SOC L1 should verify the source, affected host, user, process or request fields, timing, and related activity.
La règle signale un comportement potentiellement suspect. Le SOC L1 doit vérifier la source, l’hôte affecté, l’utilisateur, les champs de processus ou de requête, la chronologie et les activités associées.
